origin.description: Alias of assertCount. Returns the value when it is a single count, zero or more. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
origin.usage: assert_count(x, na.ok = FALSE, positive = FALSE, tol = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps), null.ok = FALSE, coerce = FALSE, .var.name = vname(x), add = NULL)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Value under test. A Python int is an R integer and a Python float is an R double.

arguments.name: na.ok
arguments.text: When true, one missing value is allowed.

arguments.name: positive
arguments.text: When true, the count must be at least 1.

arguments.name: tol
arguments.text: How far a number may sit from an integer.

arguments.name: coerce
arguments.text: When true, a passing double is rounded and stored as integer.

arguments.name: .var.name
arguments.text: Name used in the assertion message.

arguments.name: add
arguments.text: Collection that stores the message instead of stopping.

origin.details: Alias of assertCount. Returns the value when it is a single count, zero or more. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
origin.value: The value when the check passes. Otherwise the check stops.
